steps.what: Initiate classroom discussions, facilitate participation and moderate competing interpretations

tasks.design: Retain live moderation with the lecturer. Existing prompts in {DOCS} support the session without replacing the interpersonal work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discussion depends on the students' contributions in the moment.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing participation and responding to misconceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertainty and helping students explain their reasoning.
tasks.altitude: No change to teaching authority or time.

evidence.claim: Live classroom facilitation requires interpersonal and subject judgement; no labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is live discussion, excluding course material development and grading.
Students produce contributions live; no structured transcript, sentiment flag or free capture process is assumed.
Consider native teaching features before custom code; no new system is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because discussion practice remains unchanged.
research_questions: Is any repeated clerical component actually part of the observed discussion task?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Live moderation retains full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify course outcomes, source content, assignment requirements and timetable
Prepare syllabi, homework assignments and handouts from the materials brief

loop.purpose: Draft course materials from lecturer-selected content
loop.input: Outcomes, source pack, timetable and assignment requirements
loop.output: Draft syllabus sections, assignments and handouts
loop.check: Lecturer verifies scientific explanations, source support, workload and alignment to learning outcomes
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported or unsuitable material is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Teaching explanations and assignment wording require contextual writing beyond template fields

steps.what: Check course materials, solve assignments and publish the approved versions

tasks.design: Use approved drafting support in {DOCS}, then publish lecturer-checked materials through {LMS}. The lecturer retains scientific accuracy, assignment feasibility and final release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing clear instructional prose and exercises takes writing time.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can restate a verified source pack for a specified audience.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate physiology, appropriate exercise examples and educational validity.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what students need to understand and whether an assignment teaches it.
tasks.altitude: A modest writing gain can support better worked examples without changing teaching authority.

evidence.claim: Source-bounded text drafting may assist material preparation; the proposed saving is an unmeasured teaching scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers material development and publication, excluding live teaching and marking.

Lecturer captures outcomes, audience level, source versions, deadlines, workload and assignment constraints in s1; capture time remains included. Missing content requires manual research and writing rather than invented facts.
Test native document templates and approved drafting first. No personal exercise prescription or student health profiling is proposed.
Final checks include solving or walking through assignments rather than checking only formatting.
unknowns: Approved source packs and drafting environment
research_questions: Does a checked draft reduce preparation time at equal scientific and teaching quality?

incremental.description: Source restrictions and drafting template upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Final syllabus, assignments, handouts, source versions and publication destination; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=86, gross14 minus focal upkeep6 gives net8. Range allows specialist explanations and unsuitable drafts to consume the benefit; final assignment checking stays fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain student attendance and grade records

steps.what: Capture attendance and reconcile approved grades with student and course identifiers
Populate attendance records, grades and required record views from checked entries
Review record exceptions and complete required official grade publication

tasks.design: Configure record views in {LMS} from lecturer-checked attendance and already approved grades. Keep exceptions and any required official publication in the student administration system {OTHER} within the retained review step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly copying checked entries into required views can create avoidable work.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records and views can reuse explicit identifiers and values.
tasks.still_hard: Identity mismatches, disputed attendance and institution-specific official records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving discrepancies without changing an approved grade silently.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeat recording while retaining responsibility for accurate student records.

reach.learn: Official record rules and correction procedures

evidence.claim: Radboud requires Brightspace grades also to be published in OSIRIS, illustrating that required official recording can remain outside the learning system.
Configured views can reuse checked records; proposed time shares and saving are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is attendance capture and maintaining records after grading decisions; substantive grading belongs to its own task and is not counted here.

Lecturer produces student ID, course and session IDs, attendance status and source, approved grade value and assessment version in s1, including capture and matching time. No biometric attendance or free structured attendance feed is assumed.
Test native record configuration first. Missing IDs or disputed values require manual reconciliation; existing automatic record updates earn no new saving.
The {OTHER} slot is the official student administration system. Its required entry and publication remain in s3; no unsupported automatic cross-system write is assumed.
unknowns: Current duplicate entry and existing integrations
research_questions: How much repeat view population remains after attendance capture, official publication and exceptions are included?

already_counted.description: Attendance capture and grade identifier reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Student, course, session, assessment versions, attendance and grade values and official destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60, gross40 minus focal upkeep7 gives net33. Range allows existing integrations and required official entry to eliminate most or all repeat-population benefit; capture and final reconciliation remain counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review assessment requirements and capture answer keys for closed assignment questions
Score closed assignments against the checked answer key
Evaluate papers and practical work, resolve scoring issues and release grades

tasks.design: Configure closed-question marking in {LMS} while retaining paper, practical-work and open-answer judgement with the lecturer. The lecturer resolves anomalies and approves results before student release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fixed-key assignment items can require repetitive marking.
tasks.enabler_now: Native closed-question scoring applies explicit accepted answers and points.
tasks.still_hard: Evaluating reasoning, practical competence and defensible alternative answers.
tasks.human_edge: Judging quality and giving meaningful individual feedback.
tasks.altitude: A limited marking gain can support difficult assessments; grade authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Ans auto-marks closed questions and supports open-question marking workflows.
The proposed saving is conditional on closed assignment questions currently marked manually.

assumptions: Boundary covers coursework assessment and initial grade release, excluding later record maintenance and examinations.
Lecturer produces item ID, accepted answer, points, rubric and assessment version in s1, including key capture. Students submit through the existing process; no new student work is introduced.
Test native assessment configuration first. Missing keys, unreadable submissions and ambiguous answers return to manual marking in s3.
Existing automatic scoring earns no new saving; papers, practical assessment and feedback retain their full time.
unknowns: Proportion of practical and open-ended work
research_questions: What current marking time consists of fixed-answer items not already scored automatically?

already_counted.description: Open marking, exceptions, feedback and release

incremental.description: Key regression and scoring configuration upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Student, submission, key and rubric versions, item marks, final grade and feedback; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross15 minus focal upkeep7 gives net8. Zero when assignments are entirely open-ended or closed scoring is already automatic; practical judgement remains fully counted.
